findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I reviewed the three verify.md files, which hold evidence only. Each one gets the same new "Final local verification for PR 6025" section, with the earlier verification kept below it under "Historical verification". The new section does not overstate the evidence. It says no new full local test suite was run, that integrated CI is still pending, and that this blocks the PR from being ready to merge. It also says desktop GUI execution and live host behavior are not proven. The historical numbers add up: 11,534 CLI + 198 relay + 153 collector = 11,885 tests passed, and 14 + 1 = 15 skipped. I found nothing that reports success while the claimed behavior could be false. The findings below are non-blocking notes about how clear and traceable the evidence is.

The ✅ on the Gherkin and Scenarios lines covers only the two affected Claude feature files (104 scenarios). The full acceptance lane (597 scenarios) and the 51 proof-tag tests were not re-run on the integrated head. The Test Suite and Evidence limits lines say CI is pending, but the Gherkin line could be read as a full-lane pass. Before merge, the CI result at the final head should replace these partial numbers, or the line should say it is partial.

The branch-wide implement-exit phase stamp was skipped, not satisfied. The file says the skip was recorded openly and that no review was fabricated, so it is disclosed. However, the 'supported skip' itself does not appear in these files: no command, receipt ID or path. That makes it hard to audit independently. Add a pointer to the skip record.

The same 'Final local verification' section is copied word for word into all three ticket files. It refers to 'R1', the 'M1/M2' stamp and N7QY4E evidence paths without defining them in tickets 4RGYMY and 117CBF. Any future correction would have to be made in three places. Consider keeping the section in one shared file and linking to it from the others.

The Scenarios line has no status marker, while the other checklist lines have one. The 140-test unit run is also a different run from the historical 136 passed / 1 skipped run. Neither is inconsistent, but naming the commit or command for the 140-test run would make the result easier to trace.

The dependency audit has seven existing vulnerabilities (two high) and is still failing repository-wide. It is correctly disclosed, and this change touches no dependencies or lockfile. 'Dep Drift: Clean' refers only to drift, not to the audit result.
